Three queries targeting established knowledge on how operation effects depend on the surrounding cell topology in NAS-Bench-201:

1. **Operation interactions and path structure**: how skip connections, zeroize (none) edges, and convolution placement jointly determine trainability and accuracy in DARTS-style and NAS-Bench-201 cells. This covers why adding a conv on an edge matters more when a parallel skip path exists or when upstream edges are disconnected.

2. **Connectivity and effective depth**: how the presence of a path from input to output and the number of conv layers along the longest path affect accuracy. This predicts when setting an edge to none, skip, or conv changes accuracy depending on whether the upstream and downstream edges are active.

3. **Epistasis in the search space**: studies of interaction effects and architecture-performance landscape structure in NAS-Bench-201, including local search and fitness landscape analysis. This covers consistency of those interactions across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet16-120.
